title: Superyacht Finance
summary: Search-result title of the page is 'Superyacht Finance' [a][b]. The page presents superyacht finance as a specialised form of marine lending aimed at ultra-high-net-worth individuals and family offices [b], defines superyachts as vessels over 30 metres [a], and describes the loan as a corporate loan to a holding company (SPV) that owns the vessel, secured by a mortgage on the vessel and backed by a personal guarantee from the owner / Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) [a][b]. SPVs are described as typically limited companies in tax-neutral jurisdictions such as the Isle of Man, Malta or the Cayman Islands [a]. Buyers are said to commonly borrow 50-60% of the asset's value to keep liquidity for higher-yielding investments [a][b]. The firm claims direct access to over 50 lenders for yacht or business jet transactions [a]. Sibling marine pages surfaced by the same searches add: yachts typically over 20m, British/Cayman/BVI/Maltese registers, export credit for new builds, a representative example of £11m at up to 70% LTV over 48 months interest only with a 1.00% lender fee (marine finance page), and a Heesen 50m case study of $14m at 60% LTV, 10-year term, 20-year amortisation, 2.75% lender fee. Query [c] returned only third-party superyacht-finance sources with no mention of Silver Oak Capital. The page itself was not opened; everything comes from the search tool's summaries of snippets.
